summary:
The Winnebago Land Transfer Act of 2023 (Pub. L. 118-68, enacted from H.R. 1240 on July 12, 2024) transfers administrative jurisdiction over specified federal lands and places those lands into trust for the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska.

Section 1 provides the short title.

Section 2 is the sole operative provision. Subsection (a) declares that, subject to all valid existing rights, all right, title, and interest of the United States (including improvements and appurtenances) in the described federal lands: (1) are declared to be part of the Winnebago Reservation created by the 1865 Treaty between the United States and the Winnebago Tribe; and (2) shall be held in trust by the United States for the benefit of the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska, subject to the same terms and conditions as the lands described in the Treaty with the Winnebago Tribe, 1865 (14 Stat. 671). The transfer of these lands into trust operates by direct statutory action rather than through the discretionary administrative trust-acquisition process under 25 U.S.C. 5108.

Subsection (b) identifies three tracts by reference to prior federal court proceedings: (1) a portion of Tract No. 119, as described in United States District Court for the Northern District of Iowa (Western Division), Civil Case No. 70-C-3015-W (description executed May 11, 1973), situated in Woodbury County, Iowa, lying east of the Nebraska/Iowa State Line and south of the easterly extension of the north line of the Winnebago Reservation; (2) Tract No. 210, as described in Schedule "A" of the Declaration of Taking and Judgment on Stipulation and Order of Distribution filed in the same Iowa civil case; and (3) Tract No. 113, as described in the Judgment on Declaration of Taking and Legal Description filed in the United States District Court for the District of Nebraska, Civ. No. 03498.

Subsection (c) imposes a permanent prohibition on both Class II and Class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act (25 U.S.C. 2701 et seq.) on any land taken into trust under subsection (a).

The Act does not, in its text, expressly reference or amend the Army Corps of Engineers' authority beyond the operative transfer effected by Section 2, notwithstanding the caption's reference to a transfer of administrative jurisdiction from the Army Corps of Engineers to the Bureau of Indian Affairs. The Act contains no separate authorization of appropriations, no effective-date provision, and no sunset. It took effect upon approval on July 12, 2024.
